environment.description: Same Kubernetes deployment with PostgreSQL 14. The Kafka consumer service connects to the database using a connection-pooled role 'orderproc_consumer' configured through PgBouncer (transaction mode). The PostgreSQL role was provisioned via Terraform module 'cyrilgdn/postgresql' with a restricted grant set applied at the schema level. The role's effective permissions are inherited from the 'readonly_base' role group which has a default privilege alteration (ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... REVOKE ALL) and only explicit SELECT grants on materialized views in the 'orders_read' schema. The consumer's connection string references the pooler endpoint (pgbouncer:6432) with the 'orderproc_consumer' role. Note: the HTTP producer component still resolves sessions via a separate 'session_reader' role with SELECT on sessions table only. Kafka topic ACLs enforce consumer-group isolation but do not restrict produce operations from the HTTP service.

config.db_grants_consumer: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA orders_read TO orderproc_consumer; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA orders_read TO orderproc_consumer;
config.default_privileges: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE admin IN SCHEMA public REVOKE ALL ON TABLES FROM PUBLIC;
config.kafka_acls: consumer group isolation only, produce allowed from http-service SA
